bounds.domain: One existing supervisor scope, one agent and gateway, one broker and three private publications. Publication failures, cancellation, child exits, readiness timeouts and explicit cleanup failure are included. A retired scope cannot spawn again.
bounds.assumptions: Readiness is an observed authenticated result. Each startup advance either moves the finite host sequence forward or reports failure/timeout. Cleanup represents observed child termination plus broker closure, or an explicit failed cleanup outcome.
bounds.progress: Startup settles under weak fairness of the startup advance action, including timeout/failure observation. Retirement settles under weak fairness of cleanup; this permits an explicit cleanup failure and does not promise successful reclamation. The variants without fairness must have stuttering counterexamples.
bounds.limitations: Does not prove OS scheduling, elapsed deadlines, JVM/Android refinement, file publication durability, secret redaction or a physical-device speedup. One scope abstracts replacement by permanent retirement; concurrent scopes and account-store custody remain outside the model. The existing real-process JVM and loopback tests check implementation boundaries, not every generated trace.

assumptions: Weak fairness of advance, including the host sequence, authenticated readiness observations and bounded-wait failure/timeout observation. No assumption that either child becomes ready.
No fairness. A startup phase may stutter forever.
Weak fairness of cleanup. Settlement includes reported cleanup failure; successful broker closure and process reclamation are not assumed.
No fairness. A retired scope may wait forever for its cleanup outcome.
Weak fairness of advance, including startup failure/deadline or the running supervisor's exit observation. No real observation latency is proved.
No fairness. A stopped child can remain unobserved forever.
No fairness. The modeled scope is never reused after retirement.
